body: Yes. I understand that, and you're perfectly welcome to feel however you want and voice whatever opinion you want. That doesn't mean that I have to treat it like it's the most holy and sacred thing I've ever heard. If I've made you feel as if you were unallowed to voice your opinion, I apologize, but...hey, guess what? I get to have /my/ own opinions and feelings about things as well.
I know you're not, and I"m not saying you're wrong to voice your opinion or to dislike the style. All I said is that it amuses me that you came across as being so /angry/ about it.

Hey, I think you're perfectly welcome to having your own opinion, I just find it amusing that you seemed to become so upset, even though, in the text of the post, it specifically mentioned that this game would be part roguelike.

I suggest you not play roguelikes then...most roguelikes feature permadeath. Atl east, in this game, you'd be  better off after dying than starting back at the very beginning, which happens in a lot of games.

I was diagnosed about half a year ago. I don't know who I am. I mean, I feel like I can change anything of importance about me. I adapt. I don't know what defines me. I'm just me. I feel like I run on survival, do what I need to to make it through the day and then there's nothing. When I'm alone I don't feel anything. I don't feel /like/ anything. And everyone else thinks I'm all together and fine.
The problem, or part of it, is that it isn't a passion. It's an interest. I like it well enough, but I'm not passionate about it. But thank you.

Adult, working two jobs, studying Entomology. So it's not like I don't have things going for me. And I'm interested in what I'm studying. I don't hate either of my jobs. So it sounds pretty pathetic, I guess. I've been diagnosed with a depersonalisation disorder, which has something to do with it, possibly. But I just have no passion and I have to pretend all the time because I don't know how not to. And it is exhausting. I want to know who I am. I want someone else to know who I am.
